subject: use of logarithmic score; how to calculate p values to differentiate between competing models

messages.author: af6ae2e755fb46a7
messages.subject: use of logarithmic score; how to calculate p values to differentiate between competing models
parts:
Hello,
I am using the logarithmic score for model selection. However, I do not know what difference in logarithmic score would be considered significant ( such as > 2 AIC).  I found some reference that suggests permutations can be run to generate p values to compare competing models using Logarithmic score.  However, I have no idea how I would go about doing this.  Does anyone have example code of how to generate such p values?

Thanks for any suggestions

Christy Meredith

> permutations can be run to generate p values to compare competing
> models using Logarithmic score. However, I have no idea how I would
> go
> about doing this. Does anyone have example code of how to generate

I'm not sure about the `p values' itself, but

\pi(y_i | y) = E( \pi(y_i | y, ...) )

is available if you add

control.compute = list(po=TRUE)

as

result$po$po

NOTE that these values are NOT in log-scale.
